newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Taiwan wants proper treatment at Hong Kong party.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan wants proper treatment at Hong Kong party.

text.p: Taipei on Saturday warned Beijing against treating Taiwanese guests at Hong Kong's sovereignty changeover party on June 30 like officials from a province, a local Hong Kong television station reported.

"Taiwan is not a provincial government. It should be treated in a proper fashion," Cheng An Guo, general manager of Taiwan's representative office in the territory, Chung Hwa Travel Agency, was quoted on ATV station as saying.
In mid-June, Hong Kong invited 60 delegates from China's arch-rival Taiwan to celebrate the return of the British-ruled territory to China at midnight on June 30.

China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war separated them in 1949. Beijing insists Taiwan is a Chinese province but Taiwan claims China is currently administered separately by two governments in Taipei and Beijing.
Taipei says it has given approval for Koo Chen-fu, head of the Straits Exchange Foundation, to attend the ceremony but it has not made clear who most of the remaining delegation are.
Cheng said most of them would be from Taiwan's business circles, ATV reported.
One of the major headaches for the Hong Kong government was where to seat the Taiwanese.

A Hong Kong government-funded radio station on Saturday reported Taiwan saying that Koo would not attend the party if he was made to sit together with mainland Chinese as that would mean downgrading Taiwan to the status of a province.
